news.title: ‘Weekday games were amazing’: pubs toast extra £150m in World Cup sales
news.lede: England’s progress provides best football-related uplift of recent years, with one pub too packed to host its Dolly Parton tribute. Late opening hours and England’s progress to the semi-final of an expanded World Cup helped provide the best football-related uplift of recent years for pubs, figures suggest. Pubs poured 30m extra pints over the course of the tournament compared with a normal trading period, with busy pumps delivering £150m in added sales, according to the British Beer & Pubs Association (BBPA). The World Cup-related increase in sales, as fans followed England and Scotland games, also appears to have outstripped that seen during previous competitions, including England’s run to the final of Euro 2024.

news.title: FIFA letter to Argentina leaked with astonishing Gianni Infantino claim on World Cup scenes
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino is once again under scrutiny after a letter congratulating Argentina on their World Cup campaign came to light - as the deposed world champions face an investigation into the violent scenes that following their World Cup final defeat. The letter, leaked by Argentine media, was sent to Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia. Lionel Scaloni's side, for whom Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister played a prominent role, finished runners up at the tournament, beaten in the final by Spain. Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game in extra-time, before the football world was left shocked by the immediate aftermath as the likes of Leandro Paredes, Thiago Almada, Nahuel Molina and assistant coach Roberto Ayala attacked Spanish players.

news.title: Lionel Messi seen in public for the first time since World Cup final loss
news.lede: Lionel Messi suffered a heartbreaking defeat to Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final last Sunday in what was probably his final match at the World Cup. A week later, the Argentine legend was spotted in public for the first time since the loss in his hometown Rosario as he watched a fourth division match from the stands. Lionel Messi was spotted watching a football match in Rosario, ArgentinaFootball legend Lionel Messi carried Argentina all the way to their second consecutive World Cup final after producing a phenomenal performance throughout the tournament at the age of 39. However, his efforts fell short in the Final against Spain and the reigning champions had to suffer a 1-0 loss. .

news.title: Weekend Newsletter: the World Cup conspiracy Argentina can't let go
news.lede: Of course, let me start with the most important news of the week: Spain won the World Cup. Well, you shouldn't be, because bad punditry aside (and there was plenty of it) it was the logical conclusion.Football is a team sport, and that's something the Spanish have mastered, because it's a system, a school of thought, that defines the game, not a star player. The coach can swap midfielders, you won't notice it on the pitch because the structure remains: dominate passes, own the ball and ultimately score.There was something of poetic justice to it too, and I can only point you to Brazilian newscaster Bruno Cantarelli, who captured the winning goal scored by Barcelona striker Ferran Torres with the most memorable analysis of the final. O futebol vence a catimba - he shouted at the top of his lungs.What does it mean?

news.title: Japan’s World Cup Reality Check: Why the Samurai Blue Have Quietly Lowered Their 2030 Ambition
news.lede: Japan entered the 2026 World Cup speaking openly about winning the tournament. They left in the round of 32. Now, the Japan Football Association is redefining success — not as a retreat from ambition, but as an admission that the gap between confidence and genuine elite status remains wider than expected. Japanese football has spent much of the past two decades presenting itself as Asia’s most systematic and forward-thinking project.

news.title: Lionel Messi avoids suspension alongside Argentina teammate thanks to World Cup loophole
news.lede: Lionel Messi will not appear at the 30th edition of the marquee showdown. Messi and Inter Miami teammate Rodrigo De Paul have been granted special leave meaning the pair will miss the game at the Bank Of America Stadium. They fall under specific player welfare protections established by the global players' union, FIFPro. "Prior to the start of the 2026 season, Major League Soccer and the MLS Players Association agreed that upon a player’s exit from the World Cup competition, clubs would have individual conversations with each player to determine the appropriate rest and return to training and competition timeline," the MLS wrote in its announcement.

news.title: Argentina handed automatic World Cup 2030 spot as Gianni Infantino letter leaks
news.lede: The 2030 World Cup, the competition's centenary edition, is being co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco – with three special anniversary games in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay. Uruguay won the inaugural 1930 World Cup, beating Argentina in the final. Paraguay, meanwhile, is home to the headquarters of South American governing body CONMEBOL, the oldest of the six continental football federations. As such, a match is set to be held in each of the three countries' capitals, Montevideo, Buenos Aires and Asuncion.

news.title: Lionel Messi quietly made Vozinha's family's World Cup dream come true before final
news.lede: Lionel Messi reportedly ensured that four members of Cabo Verde goalkeeper Vozinha's family could attend the 2026 FIFA World Cup final after arranging tickets for them at his own expense. The gesture took place before Argentina's title clash against Spain at the New York New Jersey Stadium, where Messi's side suffered a 1-0 defeat after extra time. The story only emerged after the final, with Messi having made no public mention of his involvement. Argentine journalist Yanina Latorre revealed that Messi purchased a large number of tickets during the tournament for people who could not afford to attend matches.
